title: Twenty-four years, 33 moments
lede: From twelve kiosks to a foreclosure sale, with the money, the studios and the rivals alongside. Filter by thread.

events.title: An idea inside McDonald’s
events.text: By the company’s account the concept originates at McDonald’s Ventures, with an initial launch of 12 kiosks.

events.title: The Denver test
events.text: McDonald’s puts DVD rental machines in 104 Denver-area restaurants at $1 a day plus tax, after a smaller test in Washington, D.C. and Las Vegas.

events.title: Five more markets
events.text: The test is extended to more than 800 restaurants in Baltimore, Houston, Minneapolis/St. Paul, Salt Lake City and St. Louis.

events.title: Coinstar buys 47.3%
events.text: Coinstar invests $20.0M under an agreement dated November 17, 2005. A further $12.0M follows in December 2006.

events.title: Into the supermarkets
events.text: The Associated Press counts 750 machines in McDonald’s restaurants and 75 in grocery stores, with agreements for 400 more.

events.title: Reserve online
events.text: Customers can choose a title on the website and collect it at a kiosk.

events.title: Coinstar takes control
events.text: It exercises an option for $5.1M, goes from 47.3% to 51.0% and consolidates Redbox.

events.title: The Walmart agreement
events.text: Coinstar agrees with Walmart to expand its DVD kiosks there over 12 to 18 months. More than 3,200 are installed by year end.

events.title: 13,700 kiosks
events.text: DVD services revenue for the year is $388.5M.

events.title: Coinstar buys the rest
events.text: $162.4M in cash and shares for the remaining interests. Redbox becomes a wholly owned subsidiary.

events.title: Sony signs
events.text: A licence under which Redbox expects to pay Sony about $487.0M over the term.

events.title: 22,400 kiosks
events.text: A net increase of 8,700 in a year. Walmart, Walgreens and McDonald’s account for about 20%, 11% and 9% of Coinstar’s revenue.

events.title: The Warner settlement
events.text: Redbox accepts a 28-day delay on Warner titles and drops its lawsuit. Agreements with Universal and Fox the same year carry the same window.

events.title: Video games
events.text: Game rentals roll out nationally.

events.title: $1.00 becomes $1.20
events.text: The first rise in the nightly price of a standard DVD.

events.title: NCR’s kiosks bought
events.text: Redbox pays NCR $100.0M for its DVD kiosk business, about 6,200 active machines.

events.title: Redbox Instant by Verizon
events.text: The streaming joint venture ends its public beta and launches commercially.

events.title: Peak: 44,000 kiosks
events.text: Revenue for the year is $1,974.5M on 775.7 million rentals. Coinstar has renamed itself Outerwall.

events.title: Out of streaming
events.text: Redbox withdraws from the joint venture, citing a lower than anticipated subscriber base.

events.title: $1.50 a night
events.text: The DVD price rises by 30 cents and Blu-ray by 50 cents to $2.00.

events.title: Canada closed
events.text: The shutdown of Redbox Canada is completed.

events.title: Rentals down 18.1%
events.text: 587.6 million rentals in the year, against 717.1 million in 2014. Revenue is $1,760.9M.

events.title: Apollo’s offer
events.text: Outerwall agrees to be acquired by funds managed by Apollo affiliates for $52.00 a share, about $1.6 billion including net debt.

events.title: Taken private
events.text: The tender offer is paid and Outerwall leaves the Nasdaq.

events.title: Public again
events.text: Redbox Entertainment Inc. is created by a merger with Seaport Global Acquisition Corp. and trades as RDBX from the next business day.

events.title: 150 jobs cut
events.text: Two weeks later the annual report shows 2021 revenue of $288.5M and a going-concern warning.

events.title: Sale agreed
events.text: Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment will pay 0.087 of a share for each Redbox share.

events.title: Sale completed
events.text: The buyer assumes $359.9M of debt and signs a new credit agreement with HPS Investment Partners.

events.title: Netflix stops mailing discs
events.text: The DVD-by-mail service that began the shift away from stores ends.

events.title: $623.0M loss
events.text: The owner’s annual report for 2023 says there is substantial doubt it can continue and that it is in default on debt and leases.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment files in Delaware, with about $970M of debts and $414M of assets.

events.title: Converted to Chapter 7
events.text: Judge Thomas Horan orders liquidation. About 24,000 kiosks and the streaming services are to shut.

events.title: Foreclosure sale
events.text: The date set by HPS, the secured lender, for a sale of collateral including the “Redbox” and “Crackle” trademarks.
